practices.practice: Enforce idempotency by creating a unique index on transactionRef but only for documents that include it (use a unique partial or sparse index such as createIndex({ transactionRef: 1 }, { unique: true, partialFilterExpression: { transactionRef: { $exists: true } } })).
practices.prior_belief: Enforce idempotency by creating a unique index on the transactionRef field but only for documents that include it (createIndex({ transactionRef: 1 }, { unique: true, partialFilterExpression: { transactionRef: { $exists: true } } })) so multiple legacy/missing-ref documents are allowed.

practices.practice: Use explicit client sessions and withTransaction to group multi-document operations, and pass the session to every operation in the transaction callback (startSession() / withTransaction(), and endSession() in finally).
practices.prior_belief: Use multi-document transactions with explicit sessions: start a session, startTransaction({ readConcern: 'snapshot', writeConcern: { w: 'majority' } }), perform Transaction insert and Account update using the same session, then commitTransaction/abort as needed; treat commit errors labeled UnknownTransactionCommitResult/TransientTransactionError according to MongoDB retry flow.

practices.practice: Store monetary values using a precise numeric type (Decimal128) or integer minor-units (cents) rather than floating-point, and use aggregation/convert operators (e.g., $toDecimal) when you need decimal arithmetic in queries.
practices.prior_belief: Store money in a non-floating type: use Decimal128 (mongoose.Schema.Types.Decimal128) or integer minor-units (cents) for amount fields to avoid rounding errors and maintain consistent comparison/index behavior.

practices.practice: Create a compound index that follows the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) for account queries, e.g. createIndex({ accountId: 1, createdAt: -1 }) so recent-account lookups use an index and avoid blocking sorts or COLLSCAN.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index to support efficient account transaction queries, e.g. createIndex({ accountId: 1, createdAt: -1 }), so queries that fetch recent transactions for an account use an index and avoid collection scans.

practices.practice: Create indexes explicitly (not implicitly) before production traffic — run createIndexes()/Model.init() at startup or during CI so index errors fail fast instead of appearing under load.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes at startup (model.createIndexes()) and fail fast on index creation errors rather than relying on background/implicit creation during traffic; ensure your deployment/CI runs index creation once before production traffic.

practices.practice: Do not blindly retry whole transactions on any error; implement retries only for transient faults with exponential backoff, limit retry counts, and design writes to be idempotent so retries are safe.
practices.prior_belief: Do not auto-retry the whole transaction blindly on any error; only retry when the driver marks the error as TransientTransactionError or on UnknownTransactionCommitResult with the documented MongoDB retry/commit pattern, and implement exponential backoff with a small max retry count.

practices.practice: Reuse a single MongoClient/Mongoose connection across the process (singleton), initialize it once, and configure pool options (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize) appropriate for your runtime (serverless vs long-running).
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single Mongoose connection across the app (singleton) and configure pool options (e.g. maxPoolSize) via the connection string or Mongoose options; avoid opening/closing connections per request.

practices.practice: Keep transactions short and side-effect free — do the minimum inserts/updates inside the transaction to reduce lock contention and avoid the service's transaction lifetime limits (e.g., the Mongoose/Azure note about a ~30s max lifetime); avoid long-running business logic inside withTransaction callbacks.
practices.prior_belief: Keep transactions short and touch as few documents as possible—do the minimum update to the account snapshot plus the append insert—to reduce lock contention and RU consumption; avoid long-running business logic inside a transaction.

practices.practice: Use a snapshot-style ledger design: store immutable Transaction documents for each debit/credit and keep a separate Account snapshot document for fast reads/aggregates, updating only the snapshot in the transaction while leaving historical transactions immutable.
practices.prior_belief: Use a snapshot-style ledger design: immutable Transaction documents for each debit/credit and a separate Account snapshot document for fast reads/aggregates; only update the Account snapshot in the transaction, never mutate historical Transaction documents.

practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string from environment variables (e.g., process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit credentials to source control; prefer Azure Key Vault and Microsoft Entra ID / managed identities for production credential management.
practices.prior_belief: Read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment (process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit credentials to source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder and recommend storing the real secret in Azure Key Vault or environment variables managed by the hosting environment.

practices.practice: When creating a uniqueness constraint on an optional field, prefer partialFilterExpression or sparse:true so uniqueness doesn't enforce a constraint on documents that omit the field (e.g., unique partial index on transactionRef).
practices.prior_belief: When creating the unique transactionRef index, use a partial index or sparse:true to avoid a uniqueness constraint on documents without transactionRef (unique:false behavior for nulls is not safe); verify index behavior by inserting test docs before running production traffic.

practices.practice: Use proper numeric types in queries and updates (Decimal128 or integer cents) and ensure the ODM/driver casts values correctly when using atomic operators like $inc; avoid using floating-point Number for money.
practices.prior_belief: Use proper numeric comparison types in queries and updates (Decimal128 or integers) and ensure Mongoose casts values correctly when using $inc on balances; avoid floating-point $inc on Number fields for money.

practices.practice: Monitor request-unit (RU/s) consumption, index usage and throttling; alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation and provision adequate throughput or use autoscale to avoid throttling, since transactions and additional indexes increase RU consumption.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s consumption and index usage via Azure monitoring; provision either adequate manual RU or use autoscale to prevent request rate throttling, because transactions and large read/writes increase RU cost.

practices.practice: Avoid embedding large binary blobs or high-dimensional vectors in transactional ledger documents; if you need vector search, store vectors in a dedicated collection and create a tuned vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with separate parameters from transactional collections.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing large binary/blobs or large vectors in the ledger documents themselves; if vector search is used, store vectors in a dedicated collection with its own vector index (HNSW/IVF) and tune index params (M, efConstruction, efSearch) separate from transactional collections.

practices.practice: Enforce schema validation at the application or server level (Mongoose schema validation / server-side validators) to require fields like accountId, amount, transactionRef and createdAt and prevent malformed ledger writes.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side validators / Mongoose schema validation to enforce required fields (accountId, amount, transactionRef, createdAt, type) and types, and treat schema validation as a first-line defense against malformed ledger writes.

practices.practice: When updating an Account snapshot inside a transaction, use an atomic $inc (or Decimal128-aware increment) and perform the update with the transaction session, returning the updated document (e.g., findOneAndUpdate with session and new/returnDocument:'after') to avoid races.
practices.prior_belief: When updating the Account snapshot inside the transaction, use an atomic $inc for balance (with Decimal128 or integer cents) and use options that return the updated document if needed (findOneAndUpdate with { session, returnDocument: 'after' } in Mongoose/driver) to avoid race conditions.

practices.practice: Handle duplicate-key (E11000 / code 11000) errors explicitly in the API: translate them to idempotent success or a clear 409 with the existing resource, rather than reattempting the same write blindly.
practices.prior_belief: Handle duplicate-key errors (E11000) explicitly in the API flow as evidence of a repeated idempotent request; translate those to idempotent success (200/202) or to a clear 409 that includes the existing transaction id rather than retrying the insertion.

practices.practice: Verify indexes and query plans against the actual cluster (use explain('executionStats') or the DocumentDB MCP tools) after index creation to confirm queries use the expected index and do not trigger full scans.
practices.prior_belief: Test and verify indexes and query plans against the actual cluster (use the provided documentdb MCP server or explain()) after index creation to confirm queries are using the indexes you expect and not triggering full scans.

practices.practice: Design your partition/shard key to colocate an account's transactions (use accountId as the leading shard key when aiming to keep an account's documents on the same shard) to avoid cross-shard operations when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Design the partitioning / shard key (or logical partition key) with accountId as a leading key to keep all an account's transactions co-located and to avoid cross-partition transactions when possible; verify the provider's partitioning model and limits before assuming cross-partition transactions are cheap.

practices.practice: Keep detailed immutable audit metadata on each Transaction (createdAt, createdBy, transactionRef, source, idempotency metadata) so you can reconcile duplicates and debug failed commits without relying on mutable history.

practices.practice: Avoid TTL indexes on immutable ledgers (do not create TTL indexes that expire ledger/transaction documents); if you must expire data, keep expirable records in a separate non-ledger collection so the ledger remains durable.
